title: rate stabilizer and deferred decommit adapter
author: Evelyn Cho
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet decommits and short bursty drop-offs have caused frequent transient SLA slippage when many tenants simultaneously release reserved capacity. This PR introduces a lightweight rate-stabilizer controller that smooths sustained throughput commitments by sampling commitment deltas and maintaining a short-lived sustain pool, together with a deferred-decommit adapter that staggers decommit transactions to avoid synchronized capacity churn.

What this changes: single PR that touches the autoscaler control plane, scheduler decommit logic and telemetry so operators can observe the stabilization behavior. Key pieces: 
- autoscaler/rate_stabilizer.py: new controller that computes a per-tenant sustain budget based on recent commitment samples (EWMA + percentile guard).
- scheduler/decommit_adapter.go: replaces immediate batch decommit with a staggered commit queue that enqueues decommits and releases them in micro-batches by tenant weight and shard.
- telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: new metrics (rate_stabilizer.sustain_headroom, decommit.stagger_delay_p50/p95, decommit.backpressure_events).
- tests/cluster_sim: synthetic workloads that validate stabilization under multi-tenant bursts.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The controller avoids long-lived reservations by favoring a short (30s-120s) sustain pool that reduces oscillation without blocking legitimate capacity reclamation. Deferred decommits use a deterministic jitter schedule keyed by tenant id + epoch to guarantee progress while preventing synchronized spikes. This is intentionally conservative: when cluster utilization is low, decommits proceed faster; when utilization is high or SLOs are at risk, stagger windows expand.

Rollout plan: deploy as opt-in feature flag (autoscaler.rateStabilizer.enabled=false by default). Canary on single Dedicated pool for two weeks, monitor new telemetry and existing SLA dashboards (error budget, p95 latency). If safe, enable for all Dedicated pools over 2 days using gradual ramp.

Testing: unit + integration tests added; cluster-sim demonstrates: 1) 12% reduction in tenants experiencing >3x transient queue growth in synthetic burst tests, 2) median decommit jitter ~150ms, p95 ~1.1s for busy pools, 3) ~4-7% decrease in spike-driven tail-latency cost.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation with basic invariants and concurrency guards
- [x] Staggered decommit queue integrated with scheduler
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard patches
- [x] Unit and integration tests in CI
- [x] Canary rollout notes and feature flag

Related: ENG-7341 (stabilize reservation churn), ENG-7420 (telemetry for decommit pipeline).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Looks good overall. Main question: how do we ensure decommit progress in the pathological case where many tenants have identical jitter? Can you add a deterministic fallback that forces at least N decommits every Xs?
Evelyn Cho (author): Added deterministic epoch-based escalation (see decommit_adapter.go lines ~120-155). Fallback forces 2% of queued decommits per shard every 500ms when progress stalls.
Ravi Subramanian: Can the EWMA window be tuned per-tenant? Ops will want finer control for big customers. Suggest adding tenant-level override via annotation.
Evelyn Cho (author): Added tenant annotation support and documented safe values in docs/rate_stabilizer.md. Defaults remain cluster-safe.
Lina Chen: CI integration flake on cluster_sim; observed test timeout. Please add a retry and shorten wall-clock wait.
Evelyn Cho (author): Reduced wait in tests and added deterministic seed to avoid timing flakiness; re-ran CI.
release_notes: Introduce Rate Stabilizer (opt-in) and deferred decommit adapter to reduce synchronized capacity churn in Dedicated pools; adds telemetry for sustain headroom and decommit staggering. Opt-in via autoscaler.rateStabilizer.enabled flag.
